title: Peter Berg discusses Hancock 2 script and The Mosquito Bowl
excerpt:
Will Smith sent Peter Berg a script for Hancock 2.
Berg also discussed the antiwar themes of The Mosquito Bowl.
body_md:
Peter Berg has revealed that Will Smith sent him a screenplay for Hancock 2, offering a notable update on the long-discussed sequel to their 2008 superhero film. The director shared the news while discussing his latest historical drama, The Mosquito Bowl, and expressed enthusiasm about the possibility of returning to the Hancock franchise.

Berg described the screenplay as exceptionally funny and indicated that he would be willing to direct the sequel if the necessary circumstances came together. His comments establish that he has received a script, but they do not constitute an official production announcement from Sony.

The original Hancock earned more than $600 million worldwide and generated discussions about a follow-up for years. Smith previously mentioned a promising sequel idea during a livestream in 2025 and suggested that Zendaya was being approached for a role. Her involvement has not been confirmed in the available report.

Berg also spoke warmly about Smith and their professional relationship. He expressed confidence in the actor's talent and suggested that returning to the character could be particularly meaningful at this point in his career. The director's enthusiasm is clear, although the sequel still depends on decisions that have not been publicly finalized.

Much of the interview concerned The Mosquito Bowl, a World War II drama adapted from Buzz Bissinger's nonfiction book. The film follows college football players who joined the Marine Corps and features Nicholas Galitzine, Bill Skarsgard, Ray Nicholson and Tom Francis.

Berg's research included visiting Okinawa and learning about the experiences of the people whose lives were affected by the battle. He explained that encountering contemporary military personnel during his research reinforced his awareness of the youth of those who are asked to serve.

The director described two principles that he believes can coexist: respecting military personnel and recognizing the importance of doing everything possible to prevent war. His intention was to communicate the human consequences of armed conflict rather than presenting the historical story solely as a celebration of military achievement. Following its October 30 theatrical release, The Mosquito Bowl is now streaming on Netflix.

Before any potential return to Hancock, Berg is working with Taylor Sheridan on Paramount's adaptation of Call of Duty. The film draws on the Modern Warfare universe, and Berg suggested that Captain Price could appear, although casting remains at an early stage. That project has a scheduled release date of June 30, 2028, whereas Hancock 2 has no confirmed production or theatrical release date in the available report.
